correctness.rationale: For the half graph H_n with a_i b_j iff i<=j, k>=2, n>=3, the defining inequality for every f(v)<k is f(N[v])>=k+|AN(v)|. Its endpoint leaf-support pairs have disjoint weight L,R>=k; equality L=k forces (a_1,b_1)=(0,k), and R=k forces (a_n,b_n)=(k,0). The submitted nested-neighborhood analysis excludes weight 2k+2 when either pair equals k. Otherwise L=R=k+1 and all interior labels vanish; a_2 and b_(n-1) force precisely f(a_1)=f(b_n)=k+1. This exhibits an admissible function of weight 2(k+1) and proves uniqueness. Independent direct constrained-composition enumeration tested every labeling of weight <=2(k+1) for n=3,4,5 and k=2,3: exactly 65,694 candidate labelings checked, all six instances had one endpoint optimum, no smaller valid label. This finite test is corroboration, not the universal proof.

originality.rationale: The scalar k=2 value gamma_dR(H_n)=6 is already a consequence of Padamutham and Reddy 2020 (non-complete-bipartite connected chain graphs). The reviewed added fact is rigidity of every k=2 minimum function and the exact bound plus uniqueness for every k>=3. A published 2023 [k]-Roman general bound and 2024/2026 graph-family papers concern broad bounds/other families; from materials actually inspected they do not imply this complete specific optimizer classification. Search is not proof of novelty.
